children: Consumer sentiment declined in September, according to the University of Michigan's monthly survey, but the mood improved from the survey's preliminary reading.
The survey's headline index landed at 48.1, versus 47.8 in its initial September reading published earlier this month. That was still a decline from August, when the reading was 51.7.

"Overall, interviews reveal broad agreement across the political spectrum that the outlook for the economy has weakened since the beginning of the year," the survey's director, Joanne Hsu, said. "After particularly large declines in sentiment this month, Republican sentiment is now 20% lower than January 2026; Democrats are down 13% over the same period," Hsu said.

Consumers' inflation expectations increased, including a small rise in expectations for long-term inflation. Federal Reserve officials watch inflation expectations closely, because they worry that higher expected inflation could change consumers' behavior and make price increases preordained.
